title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review initial benchmark results, unblock infra access, and align on next steps for private deployment trial. Discussed VPC peering, service account keys, KMS integration, and preliminary latency/cost tradeoffs. Action items agreed: Redwood to run 24h benchmark with production-ish traffic pattern, Nexa to provide test dataset and grant VPC access, and security to review SOC2 docs. Next sync scheduled in one week.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share pricing sheet and security whitepaper (SOC2 certs, audit logs) - due 2027-07-02
Camila Rivera: Schedule and run 24h benchmark on Dedicated pool, provide raw logs - due 2027-07-06
Marcus Bell: Create service account, provide VPC peering details and firewall rules - due 2027-07-02
Priya Reddy: Review KMS/HSM integration notes and confirm key rotation policy - due 2027-07-05
Oliver Chen: Share anonymized test dataset (5k records) and target SLOs - due 2027-07-01
next_steps: Redwood to send security package + pricing link
Customer to provision VPC peering and service account
Run 24h benchmark with realistic traffic and share results
Follow-up sync next week to review benchmark and tune batching/quantization settings
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off - this is our weekly POC sync for the NexaHealth pilot. I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Camila from our SE team.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Hi all, thanks. Quick note - we've got Priya and Marcus on for infra/security.
[00:18] Camila Rivera: Hi, thanks. I have the initial result set from the early benchmark we ran last night, it's a small sample but shows some interesting numbers.
[00:32] Marcus Bell: Sorry just joined, connection was flaky.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: No worries Marcus. Camila, can you walk the team through the numbers?
[00:40] Camila Rivera: Sure. So the short version: with the default settings on the Dedicated pool we saw p95 latency around 210ms for 512-token sequences, average token cost slightly higher than expected because we didn't enable prefix caching for these runs. There's some noise, transcription, uh, excuse me, some noise due to cold-starts in our small run.
[01:02] Aisha Khan: 210ms p95 - that's promising. Our production target is sub-200ms for key flows, but for now if we can get consistent sub-250 that's acceptable.
[01:12] Camila Rivera: Right. We think enabling prefix/KV caching and tuning batch sizes will shave 30-60ms; Camila: and quantization to int4 for your throughput-heavy routes should cut cost by ~30% with minimal quality impact.
[01:28] Priya Reddy: On the security side we need to double-check the KMS integration and how the audit logs are preserved. Can Redwood confirm key rotation and whether logs include token-level metadata?
[01:40] Jordan Lee: Good question. Short answer: audit logs include request-level metadata, timestamps, and model/version used. We don't store customer payloads unless explicitly enabled. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and rotation policies can be aligned with your org. I'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:03] Marcus Bell: For the VPC peering - we attempted to set up a test peering last week but hit a routing rule issue, our firewall is quite locked down. We'll need a list of IPs and ports.
[02:15] Camila Rivera: We'll provide the exact egress IP ranges and hostnames; typical ports are 443 for the control plane and 5005 for the dedicated agent, but we'll confirm. Also we can support a private connector if peering is unwieldy.
[02:32] Aisha Khan: Is there a way to do an on-prem runner instead? Some of our PHI pipelines prefer air-gapped.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: We do have a Private deployment option that can be on-prem or inside your VPC. For the pilot we recommended Dedicated to iterate faster, but if security requires, we can scope an on-prem package. That's a heavier lift and will affect timelines and cost.
[02:52] Oliver Chen: Timeline - we were hoping to have a short pilot completed in 6 weeks and evaluate expansion. Is that still realistic?
[02:59] Camila Rivera: Yes, if we get the VPC and test dataset this week we can run a 24h benchmark next week and then a small user-facing trial. So six weeks is tight but doable.
[03:12] Marcus Bell: I'll work with infra to create the service account and peering details today.
[03:16] Priya Reddy: And I'll start the security checklist, but I need the SOC2 doc and details on data residency and retention policy.
[03:23] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll share the security packet. Also quick note on routing: if you want to prioritize latency we can pin to lower-cost but higher-performance variants, and enable automatic fallback to cheaper models in case of capacity events - does that fit your use case?
[03:39] Aisha Khan: Yeah, we have a set of user-facing flows that need tighter latency and some back-end summary jobs that can be lower priority.
[03:46] Camila Rivera: For tuning: we'll start with batch_size 8 and dynamic batching enabled, enable prefix/KV cache with a 24h TTL for your frequent conversations. We'll also recommend int4 quantization for the summary route.
[03:58] Oliver Chen: About the dataset - we'll provide an anonymized set of 5k records that mirror the real traffic shape. Any specific format?
[04:06] Camila Rivera: JSONL with fields: prompt, expected_response, and a label for route. If you can't strip PHI fully, let us know, we can run within your VPC.
[04:18] Marcus Bell: One more infra note - we need clear instructions for network ports and the exact agent image tag. Last time the tags mismatched and it caused timeout.
[04:27] Jordan Lee: Camila will paste the image tag and runbook after the call.
[04:31] Camila Rivera: I'll include the runbook, agent image tag, and a sample docker-compose for the on-prem agent.
[04:38] Aisha Khan: Benchmark quality - can you capture token-level timing and success/failure rates? We want to see NLU quality drop after quantization.
[04:46] Camila Rivera: Yes, we'll log per-request latency, token breakouts, and a basic perplexity/ROUGE on the sample. If you want a more formal evaluation we'll run the eval harness and return a quality diff.
[05:00] Priya Reddy: Regarding logs - do you allow configuring retention? We can't keep raw PII logs longer than 30 days.
[05:08] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention is configurable per-customer. By default we keep aggregated metrics and short-lived traces; raw request bodies are disabled unless explicitly turned on and then they inherit your retention policy.
[05:20] Oliver Chen: Pricing - any estimate on the Dedicated baseline?
[05:24] Jordan Lee: We'll share the committed capacity pricing; rough back-of-envelope for your expected throughput is X per hour - I'll put the concrete numbers in the sheet.
[05:33] Camila Rivera: For the 24h run we'll instrument both int8 and int4 quantized variants so you can compare latency/cost/quality.
[05:41] Marcus Bell: Great. I'll try to get the VPC peering staged by tomorrow end-of-day.
[05:45] Aisha Khan: And I'll coordinate internally on the dataset and stakeholders.
[05:49] Jordan Lee: Thanks. Quick recap of owners and dates: Jordan to send security + pricing by 7/2, Marcus to provide VPC details by 7/2, Oliver to share dataset by 7/1, Camila to run benchmark and share logs by 7/6, Priya to review KMS by 7/5. Follow-up next Thursday same time.
[06:12] Priya Reddy: One more question - do you support SAML SSO for the console?
[06:18] Jordan Lee: Yes SAML + SCIM for provisioning. We'll include the SSO integration guide.
[06:25] Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[06:28] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and see you next week.
[06:32] [meeting ended]
